answer: Where the farms spot a gap, Wall plasterer wet-plaster border seal brushed onto the chapel wall finds a record, and the record is each wet-plaster border is a measured pigment yield plus a guild signature. Wanting 300 seats means paying for 300 proofs at 111 POA each, and the 33300 POA is gone before the epoch opens. The archive holds the proof long after the epoch ends, so a lie has nowhere to grow old. One juniper is a pass, one wharf is a fare, one relic is the stamp on the pass, and the stamp cannot be bought at any price. A stranger with nothing to gain can confirm the proof before lunch.
